Rows marked † are quoted from PRIME Table II (5-fold cross-validation test results on PRIME's own cohort splits); they were not rerun on our splits. Rows marked `I07` Test are models of this study evaluated on the held-out test folds of our 5-fold split, as recorded in their result ledger (per-cohort SD: population SD over folds): in Group 1, separately trained single-modality models; in Group 2, the frozen tri-modal PS3-style backbone. The `I07` Val $D_0$ row and Group 3 are computed on the validation folds of the same split (per-cohort SD: sample SD over folds). With all three modalities present, TriModalSurv applies the complete-modality identity bypass $D_0$ and returns the backbone prediction unchanged, so the bypass rows are not credited to TriModalSurv and are not bolded. Avg.: SD is the sample SD across the five cohort means. Bold: best value per column within Group 3. Hyperparameter protocol: Ours (`M6-a`) uses hyperparameters selected on the validation folds, and the same validation folds are used for reporting, so its numbers are optimistic relative to the other rows; every other row uses fixed default hyperparameters (`@default`) or has no hyperparameter grid.

### table_s4.tex: Cross-modal predictability and risk-weight retention of the 32-$d$ shared component $p^{\mathrm{sha}}$ versus the 224-$d$ orthogonal complement $p^{\mathrm{res}}$ (validation, mean over the 25 cohort×fold splits).

| **Target modality $u$** | $R^2_{\mathrm{val}}(p^{\mathrm{sha}})$ | $R^2_{\mathrm{val}}(p^{\mathrm{res}})$ | $\cos(p^{\mathrm{sha}})$ | $\cos(p^{\mathrm{res}})$ | Energy share $p^{\mathrm{sha}}$ | Energy share $p^{\mathrm{res}}$ | $\rho_r(u)$ | Random $r/d$ |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| `rna` | $0.0974$ | $-0.5683$ | $0.6160$ | $0.2590$ | $0.6364$ | $0.3636$ | $0.6281$ | $0.1250$ |
| `wsi` | $-0.2492$ | $-0.4775$ | $0.3222$ | $0.0710$ | $0.7258$ | $0.2742$ | $0.6945$ | $0.1250$ |
| `text` | $0.2493$ | $-0.3124$ | $0.6545$ | $0.3186$ | $0.7015$ | $0.2985$ | $0.6800$ | $0.1250$ |

> Notes: Computed on the default `M2` base ($r=32$, $\lambda_m=0.1$). For each target modality $u$, a closed-form Ridge regressor is fitted on the training fold from the other two visible modalities and evaluated on the validation fold. $\rho_r(u)=\lVert U_u^\top w_u\rVert_2^2/\lVert w_u\rVert_2^2$ is the share of the frozen risk-head weight energy inside the subspace, $5.0\times$ to $5.6\times$ the random expectation $r/d$. For WSI, $R^2_{\mathrm{val}}(p^{\mathrm{sha}})$ is negative ($-0.2492$), while its cosine ($0.3222$ vs. $0.0710$) and $\rho_r$ ($0.6945$) stay concentrated in the shared subspace.

### table_s5.tex: Stability, faithfulness and gate utility of the residual retrieval on the validation folds (default `M2` base, $r=32$, $\lambda_m=0.1$; default `B6-LOO` with $K=10$, $\tau=0.1$, $\alpha_{\max}=0.5$).

| **Check** | **Metric** | **Value** |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| ① Stability (20 × 80% train subsamples) | Top-$K$ neighbour Jaccard (mean ± SD over 25 folds) | $0.6845\pm0.0046$ |
| ① Stability | Residual-correction direction cosine (mean ± SD) | $0.9335\pm0.0111$ |
| ② Faithfulness (Top-1 erasure) | Median $\lvert\Delta h\rvert$: Top-1 vs. random other neighbour ($n=7554$) | $0.01296$ vs. $0.00423$ |
| ② Faithfulness | Paired Wilcoxon, Top-1 $>$ random | $W=24013865.5$, one-sided $p<10^{-300}$ |
| ② Faithfulness | Mean Top-1 share of the linear risk correction | $0.2420$ |
| ③ Gate utility | Spearman$(s_{(1)}, \Delta\mathcal{E})$ ($n=7554$) | $\rho=0.1686$, $p=2.96\times10^{-49}$ |
| ③ Gate utility | Spearman$(\alpha_i, \Delta\mathcal{E})$ | $\rho=0.1647$, $p=4.19\times10^{-47}$ |
| ③ Gate utility | Mean $\Delta\mathcal{E}$ (positive: `B6` closer to the full-modality risk than `B1`) | $+0.03030$ |
| ③ Half split, $\Delta$C-index (`B6` $-$ `B1`) | High-confidence half $s_{(1)}\ge\delta_\Omega$ ($n=149$ pattern×fold units) | $-0.0001$ |
| ③ Half split, $\Delta$C-index (`B6` $-$ `B1`) | Low-confidence half $s_{(1)}<\delta_\Omega$ ($n=150$ pattern×fold units) | $+0.0049$ |

> Notes: Faithfulness removes the highest-weight neighbour (Top-1) or a random other neighbour among the Top-$K$ and renormalises the softmax weights over the remaining neighbours. $\Delta\mathcal{E}$ is the reduction of the absolute risk error with respect to the full-modality risk when `B6-LOO` replaces `B1`. The table is computed on the default base and default retrieval parameters, not on the validation-selected configuration of Ours, so that the correction is never identically zero.
